description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:963-990 — tbs_without_sct_list() parses the leaf cert via Certificate::from_der(), retains the extensions vector minus the SCT-list extension, drops Option<extensions> if empty, and re-encodes via encode_to_vec(). For precert_entry signature verification to succeed, the re-encoded bytes must match — byte-for-byte — what the log saw at submission time, modulo the removed extension and its enclosing SEQUENCE length adjustment.

The docstring (verify.rs:954-962) acknowledges this and asserts that real-world canonically-encoded certs round-trip cleanly. The integration test tbs_reconstruction_is_bit_exact + the oracle's precert-tbs-no-sct.bin oracle confirm this for one synthetic fixture, and live_log.rs confirms it against ONE captured cert from one CT log.

Risk: this is a load-bearing dependency on x509-cert's encoder being a bit-exact round-trip for every TBSCertificate it parses. Counter-examples that would silently break this:
- An issuer that emitted non-canonical INTEGER (leading zero byte) which x509-cert's encoder canonicalizes on output.
- An issuer that used implicit DEFAULTs (e.g., 'version: v1' encoded as a zero INTEGER vs omitted).
- An issuer that emitted indefinite-length encodings (illegal in DER but seen in BER-leak certs).

Per workspace test discipline ('Never write a test that uses the code under test as its own oracle'): the current test base is small. PKITS or limbo corpora would broaden coverage. Worth filing as 'add differential round-trip test against the full PKITS corpus' — if any PKITS cert fails round-trip, the precert SCT verification would silently produce InvalidSignature for that cert in production.

Suggested follow-up: epic-level task to run tbs_without_sct_list against every cert in PKITS that has the SCT-list extension OID (or any cert, for the round-trip check minus the strip) and assert bit-exactness, mirroring pkix-path's existing chain-signature verification round-trip behavior.
title: tbs_without_sct_list relies on x509-cert re-encoding being byte-identical for ALL un-stripped fields, not just structurally equivalent
